name: John Fetterman
role: U.S. Senator from Pennsylvania (since 2023); Lieutenant Governor of Pennsylvania (2019–2023); mayor of Braddock (2006–2019)
summary: John Fetterman is a Democratic senator who combines economic positions of the left (higher taxes on billionaires, a $15 minimum wage, strong support for unions, cannabis legalization, abortion rights, LGBTQ protections) with positions that break from his party, notably unusually strong support for Israel and military action against Iran, a hard line on border security, and support for AI data centers. He has said he is 'not a progressive, just a Democrat', and in recent years has openly criticised parts of his party while voting with it on most issues.

sources.title: John Fetterman VoteMatch (OnTheIssues)
sources.author: OnTheIssues
sources.usedFor: Record items: officiated same-sex marriage, clemency, legalization, $15 wage

universal-healthcare.rationale: Described healthcare as a fundamental human need and right and said he backs Medicare for All or any path to expand access (2022 campaign, as reported); no later retraction found.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His 2022 campaign mailer pledged to raise the minimum wage to $15 an hour; no later change found.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Reintroduced the Billionaires Income Tax Act, saying billionaires should pay their fair share; Wikipedia also records support for a wealth tax.

unions-good.rationale: Said 'Every worker deserves a union. Unions built the middle class and they built America' and listed himself as pro-labor in 2026.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Cosponsored the Price Gouging Prevention Act, backed an $8 credit card late-fee cap and a bill against meat-packer consolidation, framed as curbing corporate greed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Called Republican SNAP cuts 'cruel', vowed to protect and expand SNAP and listed himself as 'pro-SNAP' in 2026.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Strongly backs legalizing cannabis ('I'm not going to judge anyone for using it'); no recorded position on other drugs.

limit-guns.rationale: Backed universal background checks and red flag laws and, in July 2022, a ban on military-style assault weapons, while being a gun owner himself.

empower-police-military.rationale: Calls himself pro-policing and opposes defunding police, but no recorded call for more police funding or authority; supports national defense bills.

rehabilitation.rationale: Prison reform and rehabilitation are described as a signature issue; as Board of Pardons chair he pushed clemency for model prisoners.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Officiated one of the first same-sex marriages in Pennsylvania as mayor (OnTheIssues record); in 2026 listed himself as 'pro-LGBT'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says he is 'strongly pro-choice', cosponsored the Women's Health Protection Act and called abortion a decision for women and doctors, 'sacred and non-negotiable'.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Said the affirmative action ruling tried to 'erase the very simple fact that historical racism exists' and vowed to give kids of color a fair shot.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mixed: calls for a secure border and says an influx 'the size of Pittsburgh' came across, but supports pathways to citizenship and calls himself pro-immigration.

free-trade.rationale: Opposed the Trans-Pacific Partnership and has been described as a free-trade skeptic; OnTheIssues records his stance against NAFTA-style trade policy.

open-borders.rationale: Voted for the bipartisan border bill, cosponsored the Laken Riley Act and says 'we must secure our border'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Mixed: called the climate crisis real and embraced the green ideal in 2021 per Wikipedia, but backs a gradual transition and fracking.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Mixed: Wikipedia records he agreed tariffs could bring back manufacturing jobs, opposed the TPP and criticised tariffs on allies; in 2025 he said he did not understand tariffs on Canada and Mexico.

military-superiority.rationale: Calls himself 'unapologetically supportive of our national defense' and backs shipbuilding and defense legislation; no explicit superiority statement.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Said he rejects 'AI doomsdaying', opposed a data center moratorium as 'China First' and backs building AI infrastructure.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wrote that politics for him 'wasn't about being a Democrat or Republican' but delivering results, and says he works across the aisle.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Describes himself as an unapologetic supporter of Israel and the Jewish community and 'in lockstep' with Israel; no explicit statement on a right to statehood.

force-without-un.rationale: Urged striking Iran's nuclear sites and voted against Iran war-powers resolutions per Wikipedia; praised the Maduro arrest; no mention of UN approval.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Backed a bill to repeal the SNAP time limit on able-bodied adults without dependents: 'Food isn't a reward for punching a timecard.'

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said in 2022 'I support fracking' and that fossil fuels remain part of the energy portfolio while transitioning to green energy; no call for expanding coal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said 'Everyone in America deserves equal protection under the law' and he would not stop fighting until achieved.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Joined striking UAW workers on picket lines and urged them to 'make them pay until they pay you what you deserve'.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Voted to bar a president from withdrawing from NATO without Congress; backs allies Israel, Ukraine and Taiwan.

death-penalty.rationale: As lieutenant governor he supported the moratorium on executions and called the death penalty inhumane, antiquated and flawed (per Wikipedia); terrorism cases not addressed specifically.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Lists repeal of birthright citizenship among 'extreme policies' that the filibuster has prevented.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Backed a two-state solution in January 2024 but by 2025 said he opposed one (per Wikipedia); latest position leans against territorial concessions.

collective-defense.rationale: Voted against a 2023 NDAA amendment saying NATO Article 5 does not obviate declaring war and for Kaine's amendment barring withdrawal from NATO (per Wikipedia).

ban-cartels.rationale: Introduced a bill meant as a countervailing force against corporate concentration in the meat industry; it funds small producers rather than breaking up firms.

no-bailouts.rationale: Repeatedly criticised the bailout of big banks and their CEOs who crashed the economy ('if we can spend trillions bailing out big banks...').

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Called the Supreme Court decision restricting race-conscious admissions a 'cowardly decision' that 'upended the concept that diversity is our strength'.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Called the 303 Creative ruling 'a constitutional right to discriminate against LGBTQ people' and 'despicable'.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Vowed to do anything he could to block the sale of U.S. Steel to Nippon Steel: 'Steel is always about security'.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Said the Chinese government and other adversaries should own zero U.S. farmland and backed an NDAA amendment banning purchases by China, Russia, North Korea and Iran; he did not address foreigners generally.

corporate-influence.rationale: Per Wikipedia (March 2025) he voiced concern that unlimited money in politics harms democracy; he cosponsored a congressional stock-trading ban to curb corruption.

non-intervention.rationale: Called for strikes on Iran's nuclear sites and said the Maduro arrest was a positive development.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Says he is 'unapologetically supportive of... the trans community', voted against banning trans girls from girls' sports and condemned the trans troop ban.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Called the movement to defund the police absurd and describes himself as pro-policing; he supports prison reform rather than abolition.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Urged a US strike on Iranian nuclear facilities before any attack on the US.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Supports the PRO Act and the 'union way of life', walked picket lines and called for expanding union membership.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Called the Supreme Court's ruling against Biden's student loan forgiveness 'ridiculous' and cosponsored a bill zeroing interest on federal student loans.

voter-id.rationale: Said 'Keep it basic: PHOTO ID to vote' and fully supports photo identification; did not address proof of citizenship and opposed the SAVE America Act in current form.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Voted for cloture on a bill sanctioning the ICC over its Netanyahu warrants (Jan 2025, per Wikipedia).

close-ties-china.rationale: Said 'China is not our friend' and urged winning the 'war for AI supremacy over China'.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Cosponsored the Universal School Meals Program Act giving free meals to every student rather than only poor children.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Said 'Discrimination and racism are still real in America' in 2023.

notes: Views have shifted since his 2022 campaign: on Israel (from backing a two-state solution to opposing one by 2025), the filibuster (supported ending it, then in July 2026 called that 'horribly wrong'), immigration and the border (pro-pathway but now emphasising enforcement), and fracking (opposed in 2016-2018 statements, supports it since 2022). The most recent clear position is used. Several economic answers (health care, $15 wage) rest on 2022 campaign material with no later change found. His memoir Unfettered (2025) was not available as full text; NPR interview coverage tied to it was used instead.
